one_line: Attention is a single similarity field: A (qkv) reads it as a soft, directed convex combination of value vectors, B (simplicial) reads the same field, symmetrized and thresholded at eps, as a simplicial skeleton with Betti numbers.
contradictions: A: output is a continuous convex combination o=Sigma alpha_j v_j (every token always contributes, no threshold, always fully connected) vs B: connectivity is binary and thresholded (an edge exists only if mutual attention > eps, a combinatorial complex).

A: attention is directed/asymmetric (one chosen query token reads keys then values) vs B: attention is symmetrized into undirected mutual agreement (edge weight = min(alpha_ij, alpha_ji), needs both directions).

A: the learned projections W_Q/W_K/W_V are the mechanism (twist knobs define what is relevant/what is read) vs B: raw identity dot/cosine similarity with 'no learned weights for clarity' on fixed 3D semantic axes.
resolution: One soft adjacency field s(i,j)=(W_Q x_i).(W_K x_j): A integrates the soft row against V (content readout), B symmetrizes with min, thresholds at eps and fills triangles (topology). B is exactly A at W=I; W and the softmax temperature reshape the field while eps sets the soft<->discrete cut, so both the convex readout and the Betti invariants are functions of the same field.
viz: Theme-aware 2D canvas showing one field with two readouts at once: faint lines = soft mutual-attention field (thickness ~ min(alpha_ij,alpha_ji)), bright lines = eps-thresholded 1-skeleton, filled shapes = 2-simplices, and the selected query's output o=Sigma alpha v as an arrow. Knobs for W_Q/W_K/W_V twist, temperature T, threshold eps, and query token, with a live edges/triangles/beta0/beta1 readout. Zero external requests.
